"I want you to create a game about being a gritty, hard-boiled 1940s noir detective solving randomized murder mysteries late at night. 

Here is how the game works and what you need to build:
- Visuals @COMMENT_BODY@ Atmosphere: Dark, moody noir aesthetic with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting. Keep all text descriptions short, punchy, and under two sentences—no long paragraphs.
- Randomized Cases: Every time a new game starts, randomly generate a new Victim, a Murder Weapon, 3 Suspects (with motives and alibis), 4 Clues (including 1 definitive \"Smoking Gun\" clue that proves who did it), and 1 True Killer.
- Stage 1 - The Call: Start the game in a dark detective office with a rotary phone ringing at 2:00 AM. Give the player the crime scene address and a short tip from Sergeant Miller, with a button to [Head to the Crime Scene].
- Stage 2 - Top-Down Crime Scene: Show a top-down view of the crime scene room with 4 clickable/tappable objects (such as a desk, a shattered window, a coat, or a safe).
- Stage 3 - The Zoom-In: When the player taps an object, zoom in to a detailed close-up view of that object and reveal one clue with a single gritty sentence describing what was found. Include a button to [Zoom Out].
- Stage 4 - The Evidence Board: Always show a button to [Open Evidence Board]. On the Evidence Board screen, display all clues discovered so far, profile cards for the 3 suspects, and buttons to [Accuse a Suspect] or [Return to Crime Scene].
- Win/Loss Conditions: If the player accuses the wrong suspect, or tries to accuse the right suspect without having found the \"Smoking Gun\" clue first, trigger a Game Over screen where the killer escapes and the case goes cold. If the player finds the \"Smoking Gun\" and accuses the true killer, trigger a Victory screen where the killer is arrested.

Make sure the game is specifically designed for vertical mobile not pc, so no scrolling

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Need showScreen called after render for board/accuse. Important transitions: `.screen` transition with visibility .5s. On show, content. Fine. `renderCase` updates all IDs: ``` $('#officeCaseNo').textContent = `#${id}`; $('#millerLine').textContent = `“${tip}”`; ... ``` Scene victim: `${victim.name}` plus maybe role in sub. I have HUD sub "VICTIM — ". Set b to "Arthur Vale, nightclub owner". At 8px, could be long but max-width 230 ellipsis. Fine. Scene place: location.name. boardVictim name; boardVictimRole role. accuseCaseNo, boardCaseNo, sceneCaseNo, endCaseNo. - sceneArt.dataset.place. `renderSceneState`: ``` $$('.hotspot').forEach(btn=>{ const key = btn.dataset.object; const found = state.found.has(key); btn.classList.toggle('found',found); btn.querySelector('.tag').textContent = found ? `${OBJECTS[key].short} ✓` : OBJECTS[key].short; btn.setAttribute('aria-label', `${found?'Review':'Inspect'} ${OBJECTS[key].name}`); }); $('#clueProgress').textContent = `${state.found.size} OF 4 CLUES LOGGED`; ``` Maybe when 0 use "0 OF 4 CLUES LOGGED". Yes. Show a hint "4 OF 4 · OPEN THE BOARD" when all found? Clue progress could be. Keep. `openObject`: ``` const first = !state.found.has(key); state.currentObject=key; state.found.add(key); renderZoom(); showScreen('zoom'); if(first){ flash(); Sfx.clue(letter?); } ``` Flash via function: ``` function cameraFlash(){const f=$('#flash'); f.classList.remove('on'); void f.offsetWidth; f.classList.add('on');} ``` Sfx clue if enabled. `renderZoom`: - guard currentObject. - `clue` from caseData. - set text. - `clueSheet.classList.toggle('is-gun', type==='gun')` - gunTag hidden by CSS. - Set zoomCanvas innerHTML. Add closeup SVG. The art uses IDs; only one at a time. - set object labels. - `zoomFound` `${found.size} / 4`. - Set `zoomExhibit`: `EXHIBIT ${obj.exhibit} · ${obj.short}`. - plate. - Set `zoomArt.dataset.object`. - `#zoomArt` has `aria-label`? Set. - also log small status. - View: class .is-gun. `renderBoard`: Build HTML. Use tilt array based on object index: [-.35,.25,-.15,.4]. `--tilt`. Use `--i`. Locked cards show `CLUE 01 · DESK` and "NOT YET LOGGED — INSPECT THE {short}" maybe. Keep text "NOT YET LOGGED". Maybe "CLUE NOT YET LOGGED". Remember requirement 4 clues including gun; board shows all slots locked. - Escaping text via esc. - suspect portraits. - Suspect row maybe add no data; board list display. Fine. - If clues found, gun card red tag. `renderAccuse`: - state.selected reset when entering? It persists maybe. Set null each time to force deliberate selection. Yes renderAccuse sets state.selected=null unless passed preserve? On entering from board, reset. On clicking back from confirm, preserve. We call renderAccuse on entering; don't call when selecting. So set state.selected = null at render. Good. - HTML rows. - update button & warning after. - `setSelected(index)` updates classes, button disabled, text; ensure no re-render. - Make accusation opens confirm; if selected. - Do accuse evaluate: ``` const correct = state.selected === caseData.killerIndex; const hasGun = ...; const win = correct && hasGun; showEnd(win, {correct, hasGun}); ``` - `state.failure = !correct ? 'wrong' : !hasGun ? 'no-gun' : null`. `showEnd`: Detailed set. Classes on `#screen-end`. ``` end.classList.toggle('is-win', win); ... endStamp.textContent = win?'CASE CLOSED':'CASE COLD'; endHeadline = win?'The bracelets clicked.':'The killer walked.'; endCopy = ... endKillerLabel ... endKiller ... endVictim = `${victim.name} — ${victim.role}` maybe em dash; endWeapon = `a ${weapon}`; endNail.innerHTML = `THE NAIL ${esc(gun.text)}`; // text under 2 sentences ... showScreen('end') cameraFlash on win ``` For loss no gun: copy "You had the right name and empty hands. {killer} walked before the ink was dry." 2 sentences. For wrong: "The wrong name bought {killer} a clean getaway. By dawn, the trail was rain." Actually if wrong, the true killer is revealed but "the wrong name bought ..." nice. Win copy: "{killer} didn't say a word on the ride downtown. The city can sleep—for one night." 2 sentences. Hmm gritty. Good. Headline maybe "The bracelets clicked." nice. End weather text. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each new case randomizes a victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a definitive smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Gameplay stages: 2:00 AM phone call, top-down scene with four inspectable objects, close-up clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, and win/loss screens.
- Accusing incorrectly or accusing before finding the smoking gun loses; correctly accusing after finding it wins.
- Designed for vertical mobile with no scrolling.

## Decisions
- Built from scratch as a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Added optional user-enabled synthesized rain/phone audio; no external runtime dependencies.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented randomized cases, four interactive objects/clues, evidence board, suspect accusation flow, and victory/game-over logic.
- Built noir office, crime-scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views with mobile-focused styling.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Improve the office scene, lamp, and phone, and make the phone ring, answer on tap, and lead into sergeant dialogue.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes a victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, and win/loss screens.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office should look better; lamp and phone should be visually improved.
- Phone must ring, be tappable to pick up, then display the sergeant's dialogue lines.
- Ringing sound should be better and remain optional/user-enabled.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Office call is now interactive and gated: the scene button stays disabled until the phone is answered and Miller's dialogue/address is completed.
- Phone is a real accessible button; office content uses `pointer-events:none` with interactive children re-enabled so taps reach the phone.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, and victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- End-screen booking-portrait card styling and short-screen variants.
- Fixed `.device`/`.screen` internal focus scrolling by using `overflow:clip`, preventing clipped screens.
- Upgraded office visuals: wall treatment, window mullions/droplets/sill, richer desk, dust motes, and lamp glow.
- Replaced the lamp with a detailed SVG banker's lamp with brass frame, base, pull chain, and warm bulb glow.
- Replaced the phone with a detailed SVG rotary phone: dial, numbers, handset, cord, highlights, and shadow.
- Added ringing animation, ring arcs, `TAP TO ANSWER` hint, and handset pickup animation.
- Added `state.call` plus `buildCallLines`, `resetCall`, `renderCallLine`, `answerPhone`, `finishCall`, and `advanceCall`.
- Added three sequential Miller dialogue lines, line counter, `NEXT`/`TAKE THE ADDRESS` action, address reveal, and updated clock/kicker.
- Improved synthesized ring with metallic bell partials, tremolo, and clapper click; added pickup thunk/static.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and full Playwright flows at `390×844`, `360×640`, and `320×568`, including win path, call reset, no-scroll layout, and audio enable/disable.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Office markup, phone/lamp SVGs, call dialogue card, other game screens.
- `game.js`: Case generation, call state/flow, audio synthesis, clue/board/accusation logic.
- `styles.css`: Office/noir artwork, phone/lamp styling, responsive layout, end-screen cards.
- `fonts/`: Locally bundled fonts used throughout the game.

## Important Context
- All current changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was made.
- Key office IDs: `#phoneZone`, `#phoneHint`, `#callCard`, `#callStatus`, `#callIdle`, `#callDialogue`, `#callLine`, `#callStep`, `#btnCallNext`, `#callAddress`, `#officeKicker`, `#officeSub`, `#btnSceneLabel`.
- Call state lives in `state.call` as `{ answered, index, done, lines }`.
- `Sfx.startRing()` is gated by `state.call.answered`; toggling sound on after answering must not restart ringing.
- On short screens, answered state shifts `.office-lamp` and `.phone-zone` upward to keep them above the taller dialogue card.

```js
function renderScene(loc) {
  const scene = SCENES[loc.scene];
  const pal = SCENE_PALETTES[scene.palette || loc.scene] || {};
  const vars = Object.entries(pal).map(([k,v]) => `--${k}:${v}`).join(';');
  const floor = `url(#rs-p-${scene.floor || 'wood'})`;
  let out = `<svg class="room-svg" viewBox="0 0 400 500" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" aria-hidden="true" style="${vars}">${SCENE_DEFS}`;
  out += `<rect width="400" height="500" fill="${floor}"/>`;
  // floor vignette maybe
  out += (scene.lights||[]).map(...).join('');
  out += drawWalls(scene);
  out += (scene.wallProps||[]).map(drawProp).join('');
  out += (scene.props||[]).map(drawProp).join('');
  out += drawBody(scene.body || [200,275,0]);
  out += Object.values(scene.stations).map(st => STATIONS[st.t].draw(st)).join('');
  out += (scene.foreground||[]).map(drawProp).join('');
  if (scene.sign) out += SIGNS[scene.sign.style]({...scene.sign, top:loc.plate?.[0], main:loc.plate?.[1]});
  out += `<rect width="400" height="500" fill="url(#rs-vignette)" pointer-events="none"/>`;
  out += `</svg>`;
  return out;
}
```

const SCENE_FLOORS = {

  hex: 'rs-p-hex', stone: 'rs-p-stone', brick: 'rs-p-brick', concrete: 'rs-p-concrete',

const SCENE_WALLS = {
  paper: 'rs-w-paper', panel: 'rs-w-panel', tile: 'rs-w-tile', brick: 'rs-w-brick',
  stone: 'rs-w-stone', metal: 'rs-w-metal', curtain: 'rs-w-curtain', books: 'rs-w-books',
  pipes: 'rs-w-pipes', plaster: 'rs-w-plaster'
};

function sceneWalls(scene) {
  const wallFill = `var(--wall)`;
  const pat = SCENE_WALLS[scene.wall] || 'rs-w-panel';
  const door = scene.door || { x: 156, w: 88, style: 'wood' };
  const dx = door.x, dw = door.w;
  const bands = `
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="379" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="0" y="477" width="${dx}" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="477" width="${400 - dx - dw}" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="379" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="0" y="477" width="${dx}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="477" width="${400 - dx - dw}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <g fill="var(--wallHi)" opacity=".5">
      <rect x="21" y="20" width="358" height="3"/>
      <rect x="18" y="23" width="3" height="454"/>
      <rect x="379" y="23" width="3" height="454"/>
      <rect x="21" y="474" width="${dx - 21}" height="3"/>
      <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="474" width="${379 - dx - dw}" height="3"/>
    </g>
    <g fill="#000" opacity=".35">
      <rect x="0" y="23" width="400" height="4"/>
      <rect x="21" y="0" width="4" height="500"/>
      <rect x="375" y="0" width="4" height="500"/>
    </g>`;
  const doorArt = () => {
    if (door.style === 'none') {
      return `<rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="var(--wall)"/><rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>`;
    }
    const metal = door.style === 'metal';
    const fill = metal ? 'var(--metal)' : 'var(--wood)';
    const leaf = `<polygon points="${dx + 5},477 ${dx + 19},438 ${dx + dw - 18},440 ${dx + dw - 5},477" fill="${fill}" stroke="#120c09" stroke-width="1.3"/>
      <polygon points="${dx + 13},470 ${dx + 22},445 ${dx + dw - 21},447 ${dx + dw - 13},470" fill="#000" opacity=".22"/>
      <path d="M${dx + 18} 474 L${dx + 27} 450" stroke="var(--wallHi)" stroke-width="1" opacity=".35"/>
      <circle cx="${dx + dw - 22}" cy="460" r="2.4" fill="var(--metalHi)" opacity=".8"/>`;
    return `<rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="#070809"/>
      <ellipse cx="${dx + dw / 2}" cy="481" rx="${dw * .45}" ry="9" fill="#d9b477" opacity=".07"/>
      ${leaf}`;
  };
  return bands + doorArt();
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Now make every crime scene a visibly different place, with many varied locations, and place the room/pier number or name that Sergeant Miller says somewhere inside the scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, win/loss.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and sergeant dialogue must remain as previously improved.
- Crime scenes must not reuse the same room: "make a bunch of different places... I mean alot."
- The number/address Miller mentions (e.g. "Pier 3", "hotel room 808") must appear in the scene so each place feels distinct.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Scene art is now modular, generated from a shared renderer plus palettes, ambient props, four focal stations, body outline, and in-world signage.
- Each location maps to one unique scene composition (target: 24 locations/scenes), with station skins varying by place (desk/bar/chart table, window/porthole/stage door, coat/oilskins/apron, safe/register/locker).
- Scene art split into multiple JS modules instead of one oversized file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- End-screen booking-portrait card styling and short-screen variants.
- Fixed `.device`/`.screen` internal focus scrolling with `overflow:clip`.
- Office visual upgrade, banker's lamp SVG, rotary phone SVG, ringing animation, ring arcs, `TAP TO ANSWER`, handset pickup animation.
- Interactive call flow: `state.call`, `buildCallLines`, `resetCall`, `renderCallLine`, `answerPhone`, `finishCall`, `advanceCall`; three Miller lines, address reveal, scene button gated until call done.
- Improved synthesized ring with metallic partials, tremolo, and clapper click; pickup thunk/static; audio toggle does not restart ring after answering.
- Verified earlier at `390×844`, `360×640`, `320×568`: win path, call reset, no-scroll layout, audio enable/disable.
- Created `scene-core.js`: 24 palettes (`SCENE_PALETTES`), shared SVG defs/patterns, `sceneWalls`, `sceneBody`, 10 sign styles (`enamel`, `brass`, `painted`, `stencil`, `neon`, `hanging`, `marquee`, `tent`, `stone`, `air`), `renderScene(loc)`, `getStationMeta`, `getStationPoint`, `drawSceneProp`.
- Created `scene-props.js`: `PROPS` registry with ~35 ambient props (rug, bed, cot, stand, dresser, chair, couch, crates, barrel, rope, counter, stools, jukebox, booth, screen, rail, rack, mic, neon, shelves, boat, water, ringBuoy, chandelier, pews, cross, car, toolWall, drums, plants, plantBench, gurney, jars, piano, trash, fireEscape, puddle, column, statue, stanchions, cart).
- Created `scene-stations.js`: `windowBase` plus 18 desk variants (`writingDesk`, `barTop`, `chartTable`, `dinerTable`, `vanityTable`, `workbench`, `trainTable`, `console`, `glassCounter`, `cardTable`, `altarTable`, `pottingBench`, `metalTable`, `readingTable`, `crateTable`, `foldingTable`, `washstand`, `projectorBench`) and 18 window/door variants (`rainWindow`, `neonWindow`, `cityWindow`, `storefront`, `porthole`, `barredWindow`, `highWindow`, `frostedWindow`, `stainedGlass`, `archedWindow`, `trainWindow`, `studioGlass`, `boothWindow`, `shopWindow`, `glassPanel`, `stageDoor`, `backDoor`, `rollDoor`).
- Fixed palette CSS variables to kebab-case via `sceneVars` camelCase conversion and replaced camelCase `var()` references.

### Active
- Building remaining coat and safe station variants in `scene-stations2.js`.
- Building `scenes.js` with 24 scene specs (floor, wall, lights, props, body position, four station placements, sign style/position).
- Integrating new scene renderer into `index.html`, `game.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Verifying every scene visually and ensuring hotspots, tags, clues, and no-scroll layout still work.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `scene-stations2.js` with coat variants (`coatChair`, `coatHook`, `coatRack`, `costumeRack`, `oilskins`, `apron`, `stole`, `uniform`, `vestment`, `smock`, `labCoat`, `coveralls`, `guard`) and safe variants (`wallSafe`, `floorSafe`, `strongbox`, `register`, `locker`, `cashBox`, `cage`, `trunk`, `poorBox`, `displayCase`, `cabinet`, `cardCatalog`, `filmCabinet`, `till`).
2. Fix `getStationMeta` fallback to use a proper default map (`desk → writingDesk`, `window → rainWindow`, `coat → coatChair`, `safe → wallSafe`).
3. Create `scenes.js` with specs for the 24 planned locations.
4. Update `index.html`: replace static hotel scene SVG with `<div id="sceneCanvas">`, load scene modules before `game.js`.
5. Update `game.js`: expand `LOCATIONS`, render scene on case start, set hotspot positions/labels from station metadata, generate clue text from station `place` phrases, use station labels on board/zoom, avoid repeating previous location.
6. Update `styles.css` for `.scene-canvas` and per-scene hotspot positioning; remove/override fixed `.hotspot[data-object]` positions.
7. Run Playwright across all 24 scenes at multiple viewports, capture screenshots, fix overlaps/visual issues, then rerun full win flow.

## Relevant Files
- `scene-core.js`: palettes, room shell, body outline, signage styles, `renderScene`, station metadata helpers.
- `scene-props.js`: all ambient prop SVG drawing functions.
- `scene-stations.js`: desk and window/door station variants (coat/safe still to be added).
- `scenes.js` (to create): 24 scene layout specs.
- `scene-stations2.js` (to create): coat and safe station variants.
- `game.js`: case generation, clue text, locations, scene/hotspot integration, zoom/board labels.
- `index.html`: replace hardcoded hotel scene art; add scene module script tags.
- `styles.css`: `.scene-canvas`, hotspot positioning, scene tag sizing, responsive rules.
- `fonts/`: locally bundled fonts used throughout.

## Important Context
- All changes remain uncommitted; no commit or push made.
- Total scene files are new and not yet wired into `index.html`; `game.js` still uses the old static hotel SVG and 4 `LOCATIONS`.
- Planned 24 locations: Marlowe Hotel Room 814; Starlight Lounge rear office; Pier 9; Alcazar Arms Room 302; Blue Dahlia Diner Booth 3; Orpheum Theatre Dressing Room 2; Halcyon Warehouse Bay 7; Midnight Limited Sleeper Car 4; Radio KNOX Studio B; Golden Calf Pawnshop Shop 12; Sable Boathouse Slip 3; Vieux Carré Casino Room 6; Chapel of St. Jude Vestry; Ninth Street Garage Unit 5; Cactus Flower Greenhouse House 2; Fairview Mortuary Room 4; The Commodore Suite 1802; Rialto Alley Alley 7; Hall of Antiquities Gallery 3; Blue Note Barbershop Chair 2; Steam Laundry Basement; Ironworks Gym; Carnegie Library Wing 2; Palace Cinema Projection Booth.
- Planned in-scene sign text uses `location.plate` as `[topLabel, mainText]`, e.g. `['ROOM','814']`, `['PIER','9']`, `['BOOTH','3']`, `['CAR','4']`.
- Scene renderer signature: `renderScene(loc)` where `loc.scene` selects `SCENES[loc.scene]` and `loc.plate` feeds signage.
- Station metadata shape: `{ label, name, place }`; hotspot positions derive from `st.x / 400 * 100` and `st.y / 500 * 100`.
- `scene-core.js` palette keys are camelCase but emitted as kebab-case CSS vars (`floorLine` → `--floor-line`, etc.).
- `scene-stations.js` currently defines `null` placeholders for `coatChair`/`safeWall` then deletes them; these must be supplied.
- Existing office IDs and call flow remain: `#phoneZone`, `#phoneHint`, `#callCard`, `#callStatus`, `#callIdle`, `#callDialogue`, `#callLine`, `#callStep`, `#btnCallNext`, `#callAddress`, `#officeKicker`, `#officeSub`, `#btnSceneLabel`.
- `Sfx.startRing()` is gated by `state.call.answered`; toggling sound after answering must not restart ringing.
- On short screens, answered office state shifts lamp/phone upward to keep them above the taller dialogue card.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Make every crime scene a visibly different place, with many varied locations, and place the room/pier number or name that Sergeant Miller says somewhere inside the scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, win/loss.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and sergeant dialogue must remain as previously improved.
- Crime scenes must not reuse the same room; user asked for “a bunch of different places… I mean alot.”
- The number/address Miller mentions must appear in-scene so each place feels distinct.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Scene art is modular: shared renderer + palettes + ambient props + four focal stations + body outline + in-world signage.
- 24 locations/scenes now implemented, each with unique palette, floor/wall, props, body position, lighting, station skins, and sign style/placement.
- Station metadata shape `{ label, name, place }` drives hotspot tags, zoom/board labels, and clue phrasing.
- Scene art split into `scene-core.js`, `scene-props.js`, `scene-stations.js`, `scene-stations2.js`, and `scenes.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- Office visual upgrades, ringing animation, interactive call flow, synthesized audio, short-screen variants.
- `scene-core.js`: 24 palettes, shared SVG defs/patterns, room shell, body outline, 10 sign styles, `renderScene`, `getStationMeta`, `getStationPoint`, `drawSceneProp`; light opacity reduced to `.26`; palette vars convert camelCase to kebab-case.
- `scene-props.js`: ~40 ambient props including new `heavyBag`, `gymBench`, `washer`, `reelShelf`, `slotMachine`.
- `scene-stations.js`: 18 desk variants and 18 window/door variants.
- `scene-stations2.js`: 13 coat variants and 14 safe variants; defaults set as `STATIONS.desk/window/coat/safe`.
- `scenes.js`: 24 scene specs (`marlowe`, `starlight`, `pier9`, `alcazar`, `diner`, `orpheum`, `warehouse`, `train`, `radio`, `pawnshop`, `boathouse`, `casino`, `chapel`, `garage`, `greenhouse`, `mortuary`, `commodore`, `rialto`, `gallery`, `barbershop`, `laundry`, `gym`, `library`, `cinema`).
- `index.html`: static hotel SVG replaced by `#sceneCanvas`; scene modules loaded before `game.js`; hotspots retained inside `#sceneArt`.
- `game.js`: 24 `LOCATIONS` with `scene`/`plate`/`feel`; previous-location avoidance; scene rendering on case start; hotspots positioned from station coords and tag side chosen by y; dynamic station labels in scene/zoom/board; clue text uses station `place` phrases.
- Verified 24 scenes at 390×844 with no JS errors, no hotspot-tag overlaps, no tags outside scene, and no page scroll (`scrollW=390`, `scrollH=844`).
- Visually reviewed scenes 01–12 in clipped screenshots.

### Active
- Visual review of remaining scenes 13–24.
- Fixing observed composition issues, starting with Marlowe bed/body overlap.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/shots/all/13-chapel.png` through `24-cinema.png` and note overlaps, cut-off props, illegible signs, or washed-out lighting.
2. Fix `marlowe` bed position (move bed from `y:188` to about `y:170`) so the chalk body outline does not overlap the bed.
3. Review/fix any other scene composition issues found.
4. Recapture all 24 scenes plus full win/loss flow at `390×844`, `360×640`, and `320×568`; verify no-scroll, call reset, hotspot labels, smoking-gun accusation, and board/zoom labels.
5. Optionally increase sign top-label font sizes if location names are too small.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: case generation, 24 locations, clue text, scene rendering integration, hotspot positioning, zoom/board labels, call/accusation flow.
- `scenes.js`: 24 scene layout specs (stations, props, body, lights, sign).
- `scene-core.js`: renderer, palettes, signage, room shell, station metadata/point helpers.
- `scene-stations.js`: desk/window station variants.
- `scene-stations2.js`: coat/safe station variants and defaults.
- `scene-props.js`: ambient prop drawing registry.
- `index.html`: `#sceneCanvas`, hotspot markup, scene module script tags.
- `styles.css`: `.scene-canvas`, hotspot positioning, responsive sizing.
- `/tmp/opencode/all-scenes.mjs`: Playwright script forcing each location and capturing scene screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/all/`: 24 current scene screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/one-11.png`: example of correct clipped scene capture.

## Important Context
- All changes are uncommitted; no commit or push made.
- Local test server currently runs at `http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html` (`python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1`, PID in `/tmp/opencode/midnight-http.pid`).
- Playwright is available via runtime path `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright` using `createRequire`.
- Element screenshots during the `roomIn` scale animation capture the wrong region; wait ~1s then use `page.screenshot({ clip: await locator.boundingBox() })`.
- `previousLocation` is a top-level `let`; `makeCase()` filters out the previous location name. Test forcing can temporarily replace `LOCATIONS` and set `previousLocation = null`.
- Station coords convert to hotspot percentages via `st.x / 400 * 100`, `st.y / 500 * 100`; tags use `data-side="top"` when station y > 56%.
- Scene SVG uses `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"` and viewBox `0 0 400 500`; container aspect is 4/5.
- `window.__midnight` exposes `state`, `makeCase`, `startCase`, `openObject`, `goScene`, `goBoard`, `showScreen`, `showEnd`, `answerPhone`, `advanceCall`, `accuseIndex`, `Sfx`.
- Existing office/call IDs remain: `#phoneZone`, `#phoneHint`, `#callCard`, `#callStatus`, `#callIdle`, `#callDialogue`, `#callLine`, `#callStep`, `#btnCallNext`, `#callAddress`, `#officeKicker`, `#officeSub`, `#btnSceneLabel`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Make every crime scene a visibly different place, with many varied locations, and place the room/pier number or name that Sergeant Miller says somewhere inside the scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, win/loss.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and sergeant dialogue must remain as previously improved.
- Crime scenes must not reuse the same room; user asked for “a bunch of different places… I mean alot.”
- The number/address Miller mentions must appear in-scene so each place feels distinct.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Scene art is modular: shared renderer + palettes + ambient props + four focal stations + body outline + in-world signage.
- 24 locations/scenes implemented, each with unique palette, floor pattern, props, body position, lighting, station skins, and sign style/placement.
- Station metadata shape `{ label, name, place }` drives hotspot tags, zoom/board labels, and clue phrasing.
- Scene art split into `scene-core.js`, `scene-props.js`, `scene-stations.js`, `scene-stations2.js`, and `scenes.js`.
- Shared floor renders as a full-frame texture with wall texture only on the border frame; top-down room illusion comes from props/stations, not a distinct wall rect.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- Office visual upgrades, ringing animation, interactive call flow, synthesized audio, short-screen variants.
- `scene-core.js`: 24 palettes, shared SVG defs/patterns, room shell, body outline, 10 sign styles, `renderScene`, `getStationMeta`, `getStationPoint`, `drawSceneProp`; light opacity `.26`; palette vars convert camelCase to kebab-case.
- `scene-props.js`: ~40 ambient props; added `heavyBag`, `gymBench`, `washer`, `reelShelf`, `slotMachine`, `barberChair`, `barberPole`, `mirror`, `laundryBasket`, `beam`, `filmCans`.
- `scene-stations.js`: 18 desk variants and 18 window/door variants; back door now has EXIT plate, push bar and threshold.
- `scene-stations2.js`: 13 coat variants and 14 safe variants; defaults set as `STATIONS.desk/window/coat/safe`.
- `scenes.js`: 24 scene specs (`marlowe`, `starlight`, `pier9`, `alcazar`, `diner`, `orpheum`, `warehouse`, `train`, `radio`, `pawnshop`, `boathouse`, `casino`, `chapel`, `garage`, `greenhouse`, `mortuary`, `commodore`, `rialto`, `gallery`, `barbershop`, `laundry`, `gym`, `library`, `cinema`).
- `index.html`: static hotel SVG replaced by `#sceneCanvas`; scene modules loaded before `game.js`; hotspots retained inside `#sceneArt`.

## The game

A short, replayable 1940s noir murder mystery built for vertical phone screens. Every case
randomizes the victim, the weapon, the three suspects, their motives and alibis, the four
clues, the true killer, and one of **24 hand-drawn crime scenes**. Each location carries the
room, pier, or suite number Miller gives you on the phone.

### How to play

1. **Answer the call.** Sergeant Miller gives you the address at 2:00 A.M.
2. **Work the scene.** Tap the four marked details to log clues. One of them is the smoking gun.
3. **Read the board.** Cross-check the evidence, motives, and alibis.
4. **Accuse once.** The right name with the smoking gun closes the case. The right name
   without it, or the wrong name, and the killer walks.

Rain, ringing, and clue sounds are optional — tap **SOUND** in the top corner to enable them.

### Run locally

There is no build step and no runtime dependency. Serve the folder with any static server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 4173
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html>. Fonts and artwork are bundled; the game also
works when opened directly from disk.

## Objective
- Finish and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.

## Requirements
- Dark, rainy 1940s noir atmosphere; scene descriptions stay under two sentences.
- Every case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Flow: 2:00 AM call → top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects → clue reveal → evidence board → accusation → win/loss.
- Wrong accusation, or the correct name without the smoking gun, must lose; correct name with the gun must win.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling; office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue must remain intact.
- Crime scenes must be visibly different places — “a bunch of different places… I mean alot.”
- The room/pier/suite number or name Miller gives must appear inside the scene.
- User’s latest instruction: “Continue where you left off and finish the game.”

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled fonts and custom SVG art; no runtime dependencies or build step.
- 24 unique locations, each with distinct palette, floor, props, body position, lighting, station skins, and sign style/placement.
- Scene art modularized across `scene-core.js`, `scene-props.js`, `scene-stations.js`, `scene-stations2.js`, `scenes.js`.
- Station metadata `{ label, name, place }` drives hotspot tags, zoom/board labels, and clue phrasing.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized via Web Audio.
- Responsive compromises: board clues allow three lines on short screens; scene description remains visible at all heights using compact styling.

339: /* ---------- renderer ---------- */
340: function renderScene(loc) {
341:   const scene = (typeof SCENES !== 'undefined' && SCENES[loc.scene]) || {};
342:   const pal = SCENE_PALETTES[scene.palette || loc.scene] || SCENE_PALETTES.hotel;
343:   const floor = SCENE_FLOORS[scene.floor] || SCENE_FLOORS.wood;
344:   const lights = (scene.lights || []).map(([x, y, rx, ry, color]) =>
345:     `<ellipse cx="${x}" cy="${y}" rx="${rx}" ry="${ry}" fill="${color}" opacity=".26" filter="url(#rs-blur)"/>`).join('');
346:   const wallProps = (scene.wallProps || []).map(drawSceneProp).join('');
347:   const props = (scene.props || []).map(drawSceneProp).join('');
348:   const stationLayer = Object.entries(scene.stations || {})
349:     .map(([key, st]) => {
350:       const def = STATIONS[st.t];
351:       return def ? def.draw(st, key) : '';
352:     }).join('');
353:   const sign = scene.sign
354:     ? (SCENE_SIGNS[scene.sign.style] || SCENE_SIGNS.enamel)({
355:         ...scene.sign,
356:         top: loc.plate?.[0] || loc.room || '',
357:         main: loc.plate?.[1] || ''
358:       })
359:     : '';
360:   const foreground = (scene.foreground || []).map(drawSceneProp).join('');
361: 
362:   return `<svg class="room-svg" viewBox="0 0 400 500" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" aria-hidden="true" style="${sceneVars(pal)}">
363:     ${SCENE_DEFS}
364:     <rect width="400" height="500" fill="url(#${floor})"/>
365:     ${lights}
366:     ${sceneWalls(scene)}
367:     ${wallProps}
368:     ${props}
369:     ${sceneBody(scene.body || [200, 275, 0])}
370:     ${stationLayer}
371:     ${foreground}
372:     ${sign}
373:     <rect width="400" height="500" fill="url(#rs-vignette)" pointer-events="none"/>
374:   </svg>`;
375: }

377: function drawSceneProp(p) {
378:   if (!p || !p.p) return '';
379:   const fn = PROPS[p.p];
380:   return fn ? fn(p) : '';

21: ## The game
22: 
23: A short, replayable 1940s noir murder mystery built for vertical phone screens. Every case
24: randomizes the victim, the weapon, the three suspects, their motives and alibis, the four
25: clues, the true killer, and one of **24 hand-drawn crime scenes**. Each location carries the
26: room, pier, or suite number Miller gives you on the phone.
27: 
28: ### How to play
29: 
30: 1. **Answer the call.** Sergeant Miller gives you the address at 2:00 A.M.
31: 2. **Work the scene.** Tap the four marked details to log clues. One of them is the smoking gun.
32: 3. **Read the board.** Cross-check the evidence, motives, and alibis.
33: 4. **Accuse once.** The right name with the smoking gun closes the case. The right name
34:    without it, or the wrong name, and the killer walks.
35: 
36: Rain, ringing, and clue sounds are optional — tap **SOUND** in the top corner to enable them.
37: 
38: ### Run locally
39: 
40: There is no build step and no runtime dependency. Serve the folder with any static server:
41: 
42: ```bash
43: python3 -m http.server 4173
44: ```
45: 
46: Then open <http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html>. Fonts and artwork are bundled; the game also
47: works when opened directly from disk.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game with randomized 1940s murder mysteries, now specifically ensuring the zoom-in is a real camera animation and every close-up is the exact object shown in the crime scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, rainy 1940s noir atmosphere; scene descriptions under two sentences.
- Every case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Flow: 2:00 AM call → top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects → clue reveal → evidence board → accusation → win/loss.
- Wrong accusation, or correct name without the smoking gun, must lose; correct name with the gun must win.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling; office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue must remain intact.
- 24 visibly distinct crime scenes; Miller’s room/pier/suite name must appear inside each scene.
- User’s latest instruction: “Improve the Zoom in feature, make it an actual animation that zooms in, and then also the zoomed in object should look like how it looked before it was zoomed in… each zoomed in object should fit its zoomed out object, like the windows… the clothes, the tables and all the objects, so work on it to make it look good.”

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled fonts/SVG art; no build step or runtime dependencies.
- Replaced four generic reusable close-up illustrations with a procedural close-up camera that crops the actual rendered scene SVG around the selected station.
- Push-in transition uses a cloned scene SVG in a fixed overlay, scaling/translating from the scene canvas to the exact close-up station rect, then crossfading into the zoom screen.
- Transition now measures the selected station’s live bounding rect on both the room clone and the close-up copy and matches size/center exactly, absorbing SVG slice rounding.
- Close-up screen measures the final `#zoomCanvas` aspect after filling clue copy (long clues resize the sheet/bay), so `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"` never crops the object.
- Close-up keeps the full-scene crop but adds a soft, masked “lens shade” that preserves the inspected object’s brightness while darkening the room around it; removed wash-out glows and garment weave.
- Applied the same `saturate(.95) contrast(1.02) brightness(1.1)` grade to `.closeup-svg` as `.room-svg` so object colors match the scene.
- Easing changed to `cubic-bezier(.3,.16,.12,1)` over 700ms with a 250/280ms crossfade and cleanup at 270ms.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized via Web Audio.
- Responsive compromises retained: board clues allow three lines on short screens; scene description stays visible at all heights.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full randomized case engine, clue logic, evidence board, accusation, win/loss/no-gun outcomes.
- 24 finished crime scenes with unique art and address signage matching Miller’s address.
- Office/call experience, optional sound, close-up, board, accusation, and end screens.
- Prior visual fixes: chapel rug, casino stand/chair, radio “STUDIO B,” enlarged sign labels, redrawn generic chair, iOS meta tags, README.
- Procedural close-up renderer (`scene-closeups.js`) with `renderCloseup()`, `getCloseupFrame()`, `closeupDust()`, focus mask, soft vignette, dust, and `.closeup-svg` color grade.
- Camera push-in implemented: `beginZoomIn()`/`cancelZoomTransit()`, transit overlay markup/CSS, dynamic `MAGNIFIED · NX` caption, reduced-motion fallback verified.
- Removed old unused `CLOSEUPS` art block from `game.js`; stations expose `data-station` in `scene-core.js`.
- Fixed bay aspect measurement: 96/96 close-ups now match bay aspect and contain the station with no clipping.
- Verified exact end-of-push-in alignment: 96/96 checks matched station center/size within ~0.1px.
- Visually audited all 24 scenes × 4 objects via full contact sheets; porthole, high windows, storefronts, stage doors, coats, tables, safes, cabinets, lockers, and costume racks all match their scene objects.
- All QA passes: `flow.mjs` 175/175, `scenes.mjs` 24/24, `invariants.mjs` 600 cases, 96/96 close-up audit with no errors, file:// launch verified, reduced-motion path verified.
- README documents gameplay, local run, and the fact close-ups are cropped from the same scene drawing.

### Active
- Final visual/QA review of the zoom feature; no further rework currently identified.

### Blocked
- Firefox and WebKit are unavailable in this environment; Chromium is fully testable.

## Next Move
1. If desired, review `/tmp/opencode/shots/closeup-sheet-{1..4}.png` and `/tmp/opencode/shots/focus/*.png` once more for subjective polish.
2. Optionally add a reverse zoom-out animation from close-up back to the scene; not requested.
3. Do not commit or push unless the user asks.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-closeups.js`: procedural close-up renderer, focus mask, crop framing.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/game.js`: `renderZoom`, `openObject`, `beginZoomIn`, `cancelZoomTransit`, screen flow.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/styles.css`: zoom/transit styling, `.closeup-svg` grade, responsive/no-scroll rules.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-core.js`: scene renderer; station groups wrapped with `data-station`.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/index.html`: zoom markup, transit overlay, script loading.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scenes.js`: 24 scene layouts and station selections.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-stations.js`: desk/window station art.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-stations2.js`: coat/safe station art.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-props.js`: shared furniture/ambient props.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/README.md`: gameplay/local-run/zoom documentation.
- `/tmp/opencode/flow.mjs`: 5-viewport, 175-check end-to-end flow suite.
- `/tmp/opencode/audit-closeups.mjs`: 96 close-up screenshot/geometry audit.
- `/tmp/opencode/alignment-check.mjs`: 96-check end-of-transition alignment audit.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/`: final close-up, contact sheet, focus, animation, and flow captures.

## Important Context
- Server: `http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html`; restart with `python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1` if refused; PID file `/tmp/opencode/midnight-http.pid`.
- Playwright runtime: `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright` via `createRequire`.
- `/tmp/opencode` may reset between turns; QA scripts may need rebuilding.
- Git: prior game work is in harness commits (`6ac9e75`, `f15b55a`, `060a42d`, “Save source and v2 conversation for issue #3”); current uncommitted files include `README.md`, `index.html`, `scene-props.js`, `styles.css`, `scene-core.js`, `scene-closeups.js`, and `game.js`. No manual commit or push.
- `window.__midnight` exposes `state`, `makeCase`, `startCase`, `openObject`, `goScene`, `goBoard`, `showScreen`, `showEnd`, `answerPhone`, `advanceCall`, `accuseIndex`, `Sfx`.
- Scene SVG uses viewBox `0 0 400 500`, `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"`, 4/5 container.
- Zoom canvas aspect varies by viewport and clue length; `renderZoom()` must fill copy before measuring `#zoomCanvas`.
- Transition overlay is `.zoom-transit` / `#zoomTransit`, frame `#zoomTransitFrame`, veil `.zoom-transit-veil`; z-index 70, below global grain/vignette.
- Reduced-motion users skip the animated push-in; `prefersReducedMotion()` checked in `beginZoomIn()`.
- `MAGNIFIED · NX` is computed from bay width / crop width relative to scene display; values range roughly 2–5X.

The zoom is finished and verified. The push-in now lands on the exact same object, at the exact same size and position, before the close-up takes over.

**What changed**

- `game.js`
  - `beginZoomIn()` measures the selected station’s live rect in both the room snapshot and the close-up copy, then animates the camera to that rect. SVG slicing/rounding can no longer cause a jump.
  - Camera motion runs 700ms with a slower, more cinematic ease, a soft veil, and a 250/280ms crossfade.
  - `renderZoom()` fills the clue copy before measuring the camera bay, so long clues cannot crop the object.
  - Removed the old generic per-object close-up illustrations entirely.
- `scene-closeups.js`
  - Close-ups are cropped directly from the rendered crime-scene SVG.
  - Added a feathered lens-shade mask: the inspected object keeps its scene brightness while the surrounding room falls into shadow.
  - Removed glow washes, garment weave overlays, and heavy background blur.
- `styles.css`
  - `.closeup-svg` uses the same color grade as the room (`.room-svg`), so brass, wood, fabric, and glass match.
  - Removed the final zoom-screen scale animation that caused a visible pop.
- `README.md`
  - Documents that close-ups are cropped from the same scene drawing.

**Verification**

- 96/96 close-ups: no clipping, matching bay aspect, station present.
- 96/96 transition endpoints: station center and size match the settled close-up within ~0.1px.
- All 24 scenes × 4 objects visually audited against their source rooms (portholes, high windows, storefronts, stage doors, coats, tables, safes, lockers, racks).
- `flow.mjs`: 175/175 across five viewports, including the 320×568 no-scroll case.
- `scenes.mjs`: 24/24, no problems.
- `invariants.mjs`: 600 randomized cases valid.
- `file://` launch and reduced-motion fallback both pass with no console errors.

Final captures are at `/tmp/opencode/shots/final-scene.png` and `/tmp/opencode/shots/final-zoom.png`; the full audit sheets are `/tmp/opencode/shots/closeup-sheet-{1..4}.png`. No commit or push was made.
